version.changelog: Surface Site access control (link, password, restricted invite-only access) prominently for agents: activation triggers, capability line, and a minimal access control section pointing to https://here.now/docs#access-control. No runtime/script changes.

llm.summary: This appears to be a cloud Drive and publishing skill, but it handles persistent cloud storage, sharing, and local API-key storage with scoping and consent gaps users should review carefully.

dimensions.detail: The described capabilities generally fit a here.now Drive/publishing skill: uploading, hosting, sharing, importing/exporting, and continuing work across sessions are purpose-aligned. The same capabilities are high-impact because they can expose private files, plans, research, memory, and code to remote storage or web publishing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The trigger phrases include broad requests such as sharing, generating a URL, storing for later, and creating a webpage, which could activate cloud upload or publication flows when the user may have intended local handling. The private/password-protected wording also needs clear confirmation because unsupported privacy controls or token-sharing semantics can materially affect visibility.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The supplied evidence points to Markdown instructions and curl-based API workflows rather than hidden install scripts or executable payloads. However, the skill does not appear to declare its network, shell, filesystem, credential, and storage requirements prominently enough for pre-install gating.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Sending the user's email to here.now for authentication is coherent for login, but the workflow also has the agent handle a one-time code and resulting API key. That is sensitive and should require explicit consent, transcript hygiene, and a least-privilege alternative where possible.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact-backed workflow instructs local persistence of an API key and promotes persistent remote storage across sessions and tools. That is not inherently malicious, but it needs clearer user opt-in, retention/deletion guidance, and warnings against storing secrets or sensitive content.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review this before installing if you may use it with private files, credentials, research, code, or agent memory. Use it only when you intentionally want content sent to here.now, stored remotely, shared with other agents, or published on the web. Do not provide secrets unless you understand where the API key and uploaded content will persist and how to delete or revoke them.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: The network/API and shell-command use is expected for a cloud Drive integration, but the lack of prominent capability declaration is a real transparency concern for this high-impact workflow.
[TP4] unexpected: Drive lifecycle operations, anonymous publishing, token sharing, and privacy semantics are central to user risk and appear under-described relative to the top-level skill framing.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad triggers are concerning because ordinary requests like sharing or generating a URL could route content into cloud storage or public hosting without a sufficiently explicit user decision.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Persistent storage for memory, plans, research, and code is purpose-aligned but sensitive; the artifact needs a more prominent remote-storage and retention warning.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Local API-key persistence and agent-mediated OTP/API-key handling are materially sensitive and appear to lack explicit opt-in and safe storage guidance.
[E1] expected: Sending an email address to here.now is expected for authentication, but it should be disclosed immediately before the request is made.
[RA2] expected: Cross-session persistence is an advertised feature, but users should have explicit confirmation and deletion controls before agent context is copied into long-lived remote storage.
